messages.system: You write finite postfix programs. Follow the output contract exactly.

messages.user:
Return ONLY a postfix stack program, one opcode per line, ending with finish.
There are no Julia expressions, comments, Markdown fences, explanations or loops.
Push opcodes: x0 (current), x_prev_periodic, x_next_periodic,
x_prev_clamped, x_next_clamped, zero, one, two, half.
Unary opcodes: neg, square. Binary opcodes: add, sub, mul, min, max.
A binary operation pops right operand b, then left operand a, and pushes a OP b.
finish requires exactly one stack value and ends the program. Maximum stack depth8;
a normal budget of32 non-finish operations. At that budget you may only use binary operations to reduce the existing stack to one value, then finish. Those final reductions can bring the total to39 non-finish operations. No new pushes or unary operations are allowed during that closure. Choose all arithmetic and neighbor accesses yourself.
Input x is a one-dimensional Float32 array of length n. Periodic indices wrap;
clamped indices stop at the first/last element. Empty inputs produce no outputs.
The trusted framework supplies iteration, bounds checking and one output store.

The stack starts EMPTY; x0 is not implicitly present and need not be pushed
unless the calculation needs it. The constants zero/one/two/half are pushes,
not multiplications. To multiply a value by half, push half THEN use mul.
Generic constant-only illustration (not the requested stencil):
two

finish
